title: Constant-rate quantum codes with low-weight stabilizers and full logical Clifford actions via transversal and fold-transversal gates
authors: Takaya Matsuura, Yohji Chin, Shohei Kiryu, Kosuke Fukui
abstract: Low-space-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation requires not only high-rate quantum error-correcting codes but also space-efficient implementations of logical operations. Transversal and fold-transversal gates are promising since they limit error propagation and require no additional qubits. However, the logical operations they enable are typically restricted, and a central challenge is to construct codes that combine a complete set of logical Clifford gates with favorable code parameters. In this work, we introduce a family of quantum codes with an asymptotically constant encoding rate and sublogarithmically growing stabilizer weight, while supporting the entire logical Clifford group using only transversal and fold-transversal gates. Our construction is based on classical codes whose code spaces are absolutely irreducible Steinberg modules of their Tanner-graph automorphism groups. Taking hypergraph products of these classical codes yields quantum codes for which all logical Clifford operations can be synthesized from a fixed set of transversal and fold-transversal gates. Moreover, the slow growth of the stabilizer weight enables a high error-correcting performance in small instances. These results provide a path toward fault-tolerant quantum computation with low space overhead using transversal and fold-transversal gates.
summary: This paper presents a novel family of quantum error-correcting codes designed for fault-tolerant quantum computation. These codes maintain a constant encoding rate and feature sublogarithmically growing stabilizer weights. Crucially, they support all logical Clifford operations using only efficient transversal and fold-transversal gates.
main_problem: The central challenge is constructing quantum error-correcting codes that simultaneously achieve a constant encoding rate, sublogarithmic stabilizer weight, and support for the entire logical Clifford group using only transversal and fold-transversal gates.
main_result: The authors introduce a family of quantum codes, derived from Steinberg modules via hypergraph products, that achieve this combination, providing a path toward fault-tolerant quantum computation with low space overhead.
method: The construction relies on classical codes whose spaces are absolutely irreducible Steinberg modules of their Tanner-graph automorphism groups, which are then combined using the hypergraph product.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum CSS codes constructed using the hypergraph product of classical codes derived from Steinberg codes associated with finite groups of Lie type (Chevalley groups).
key_observables: Constant encoding rate, sublogarithmically growing stabilizer weight ($w = (\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}$), and the ability to generate the full logical Clifford group.
important_parameters: The construction requires the code to be derived from Steinberg codes and involves the analysis of group theory structures (e.g., Tits buildings, BN-pairs).
main_assumptions: The construction assumes the existence of specific algebraic structures (Steinberg modules) and relies on the properties of transversal and fold-transversal gates for gate synthesis.

paper_structure: The paper builds upon the need for codes with specific parameter regimes, detailing the construction based on Steinberg codes and the hypergraph product, and demonstrating the resulting gate set capabilities.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, mathematically rigorous construction for fault-tolerant quantum computation that addresses the critical trade-off between code rate, stabilizer weight, and native gate set complexity.
